responsibility.value: Orchestrates valid state transitions for instrument rental lifecycles. Accepts a rental entity, a trigger, and contextual data; validates the transition against a static table of business-rule-guarded transitions; and mutates the rental entity on success.

Owns: Rental lifecycle state transition rules — defining which (from-status, trigger, actor) combinations are valid
Transition-side validation via guard lambdas — instrument active checks, lock conflict checks, pickup/return gating
Transient error handling — catching BusinessException from guards and converting to Result.Failure
Audit field population — setting UpdatedById on every successful transition
doesNotOwn: Persistence of the rental entity after mutation — caller's responsibility
User authentication and authorization — actor identity is passed in, not verified here
Instrument lock management — conflict flag is passed in, not computed here
Notification dispatching — no event publishing after transitions
Database transactions or unit of work scoping
contracts: Every transition is validated by its guard before the Apply lambda executes — if the guard throws BusinessException, the entity is never mutated.
Fire never throws to the caller. BusinessException from guards is caught and returned as Result.Failure. Unexpected exceptions propagate.
All successful transitions apply ApplyAuditFields to set UpdatedById on the rental entity.

A descriptive error message is always returned for invalid transitions — either state-specific or a generic access-denied message depending on whether the trigger+actor combination is valid for any state.
assumptions: At most one TransitionDefinition exists for any (From, Trigger, Actor) tuple — FirstOrDefault picks the first if duplicates exist.
Actor authorization has already been enforced by the caller — the state machine only checks that the actor is in the allowed set, not that the caller IS that actor.
Instrument lock conflict detection runs externally and its result is passed via RentalTransitionContext.HasInstrumentLockConflict.
IClock implementation is thread-safe and returns monotonically non-decreasing UTC time.
InstrumentRental entity methods (Approve, Reject, Cancel, Pickup, Complete, ReturnEarly) are safe to call once per valid transition.
Persistence of mutated state is the caller's responsibility after a successful Fire.
invariants: The transition table is immutable for the lifetime of the process — created once via a static readonly field initialized by CreateTransitions().
Every transition's Guard (if non-null) executes before its Apply — if Guard throws, Apply is skipped.
The class is sealed and cannot be subclassed, ensuring transition logic cannot be overridden via inheritance.
A null transition lookup always produces a descriptive error — either a state-specific message (if the trigger+actor combination exists for any state) or a generic access-denied message.
failureModes: Invalid transition requested for the current rental status — returns Result.Failure with a state-specific message.
Access denied — the actor is not in the allowed set for any transition with the given trigger.
Instrument lock conflict — guard throws BusinessException, caught and returned as failure.
Instrument inactive — guard throws BusinessException, caught and returned as failure.
architecturalNotes: Uses primary constructor injection for IClock — clean, minimal DI surface.
Transitions are defined as a static collection initialized inline, making the complete state graph visible in a single expression.
The guard/apply pattern cleanly separates validation from mutation — guards can throw BusinessException without side effects.
